'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sino-Indian border dispute]]
**[[China]] and [[India]] will withdraw troops around [[Pangong Lake]] in a disputed area of eastern [[Kashmir]] following sustained talks between the two countries. Tensions have been high since [[2020 China–India skirmishes|border clashes]] last year killed dozens. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-india-56021141 (BBC News)]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (2015–present)|Kurdish-Turkish conflict]]
**Three [[Turkish Land Forces|Turkish soldiers]] are killed by [[PKK]] [[separatist]]s in [[Iraqi Kurdistan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/2/11/three-turkish-soldiers-killed-in-northern-iraq (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Four [[Pakistan Army|Pakistani]] soldiers and four militants are killed in an attack on a security outpost in [[South Waziristan]], according to the [[Inter Services Public Relations]]. [https://pakobserver.net/four-pakistani-soldiers-martyred-in-south-waziristan-terrorist-attack/ (''Pakistan Observer'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on aviation]]
***[[France]]'s [[Government of France|government]] cancels a plan by international airport operator [[Groupe ADP]] to expand [[Charles de Gaulle Airport]], the [[List of the busiest airports in France|country's largest airport]], citing reduced traffic due to the [[pandemic]] and inconsistency with environmental policies. [https://amp.rfi.fr/en/business-and-tech/20210211-france-to-scrap-paris-airport-expansion-minister (AFP via RFI)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]], [[COVID-19 recession]]
***[[Malaysia]]'s [[gross domestic product|GDP]] [[Recession|contracts]] 5.6% in 2020, its worst annual contraction since 1998 following the [[1997 Asian financial crisis]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/malaysias-economy-shrinks-faster-than-expected-in-q4-on-tighter-covid-19-curbs#:~:text=Overall%20GDP%20shrank%20by%205.6,cent%20GDP%20growth%20in%202019. (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Six people are killed and at least 65 others are injured during a 133-vehicle accident following [[freezing rain]] near [[Fort Worth, Texas]], United States. [https://www.nbcdfw.com/news/traffic/traffic-updates-overnight-sleet-turns-north-texas-roads-into-sheets-of-ice/2548822/ (KXAS-TV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Croatia|Prime Minister]] [[Andrej Plenković]] announces a slight easing of restrictions beginning on February 16, citing the stable number of new cases in the past few weeks. Foreign language schools, casinos, gyms and betting shops can reopen and restaurants and bars can also sell coffee to go. [https://www.thenationalherald.com/coronavirus/arthro/croatia_announced_slight_easing_of_covid_19_restrictions-1776758/ (''The National Herald'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Chamber of Deputies of the Czech Republic|Chamber of Deputies]] votes down an appeal by [[Prime Minister of the Czech Republic|Prime Minister]] [[Andrej Babiš]] to extend the [[state of emergency]] beyond February 14.  [https://english.radio.cz/state-emergency-end-february-14-8708145 (Radio Prague International)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] will close its border with the [[Czech Republic]] and [[Austria]]'s [[Tyrol (state)|Tyrol]] region beginning on the evening of February 14 because of a high risk of [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/02/11/germany-to-reinstate-border-controls-over-coronavirus-variant (Eurozone)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro]]
****[[Montenegro]]'s Institute for Medicines and Medical Devices approves the purchases of [[Russia]]’s [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] vaccine. [https://www.vijesti.me/vijesti/drustvo/511631/izdata-saglasnost-za-sputnjik-v (''Vijesti'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****The [[Assembly of the Republic (Portugal)|Assembly of the Republic]] votes to extend its [[state of emergency]], allowing the [[Government of Portugal|government]] to extend its second [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until March 1. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/portuguese-firefighters-jabs-virus-deaths-stay-high-75829064 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****The [[Government of Slovenia|government]] announces that starting from February 15, all [[retail store]]s will be allowed to reopen and customers will no longer need to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing]] result to enter. Schools and universities will also be allowed to resume their classes. Also, skiers will now be allowed to present negative test results from the past seven days instead of just the past 24 hours. [https://www.total-slovenia-news.com/lifestyle/7770-all-stores-reopening-primary-school-classes-restarting-monday-end-to-schengen-border-controls (Total Slovenia News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[President of Turkey|President]] [[Recep Tayyip Erdoğan]] and health workers across the [[Turkey|country]] receive their second doses of [[COVID-19 vaccine]] as the country begins to administer second doses of [[Sinovac]]'s [[CoronaVac]] vaccine. [https://www.dailysabah.com/turkey/2nd-shot-at-hope-turkey-starts-new-round-of-covid-vaccine-drive/news (''Daily Sabah'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
****[[Morocco]] receives their second shipment of four million doses of [[Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|AstraZeneca]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from [[India]].  [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/2799431/morocco-receives-4-mln-doses-astrazeneca-vaccine-india (Asharq Al-Awsat)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[President of South Africa|President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] announces that the [[South Africa|country]] has secured nine million doses of [[Johnson & Johnson]]'s [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], with the first shipment of 80,000 doses arriving next week. [https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/9-million-johnson-johnson-coronavirus-vaccine-doses-secured-ramaphosa/ (SABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] purchases 600,000 doses of [[Sinopharm]] vaccine, in addition to 200,000 doses donated by [[China]]. These vaccines are expected to arrive at the beginning of March. [https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/africa/2021-02-11-zimbabwe-purchases-600000-sinopharm-covid-19-vaccinations/ (''TimesLive'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[California]] surpasses [[New York (state)|New York]] as the [[U.S. state]] with the highest number of COVID-19 deaths. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/california-covid-19-death-toll-surpasses-new-york/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Illinois]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant in a person from [[Rock Island, Illinois|Rock Island]]. [https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/illinois-reports-first-case-of-south-african-covid-19-variant/2436094/ (WMAQ-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Carolina]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[North Carolina]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant an adult in the central part of the state who had no travel history. [https://www.wral.com/coronavirus/first-case-of-south-african-coronavirus-variant-found-in-north-carolina/19522467/ (WRAL-TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ohio]]
****[[Governor of Ohio|Ohio Governor]] [[Mike DeWine]] lifts a statewide curfew from 10:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. [[Eastern Time|EST]], citing drop of COVID-19 cases. [https://patch.com/ohio/across-oh/statewide-curfew-lifted-ohio-coronavirus-cases-drop (Patch.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]], [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****[[Washington, D.C.]] confirms its first cases of the [[501.V2 variant]] from [[South Africa]] and the [[Lineage B.1.1.7|UK variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/covid-variants-found-in-first-4-patients-in-dc/2571064/ (WRC-TV)]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] announces that [[Presidency of Joe Biden|his administration]] has finalized a deal purchasing a total of 200 million [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] doses from [[Moderna]] and [[Pfizer]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/joe-biden/biden-administration-finalizes-deal-200-million-vaccine-doses-pfizer-moderna-n1257560 (NBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[South Australia]] tightens its border restrictions with [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] due to an increase in [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases in Victoria. Travelers from [[Melbourne]] will be banned from entering South Australia, though people living in other parts of the state will still be permitted to cross the border. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-10/sa-implements-melbourne-coronavirus-border-closure/13141266 (ABC Australia)]
*The [[Democratic Republic of Congo]] reports its second death of the [[Ebola]] virus outbreak in [[North Kivu]] province. [https://www.npr.org/2021/02/11/966759228/second-victim-dies-of-ebola-in-congo-marking-viruss-return (NPR)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–Russia relations]]
**[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] expresses his support for [[President of Russia|Russian President]] [[Vladimir Putin]] as both men face protests. He also criticized the [[2020–2021 Belarusian protests|protests]] in his own [[Belarus|country]] as a "rebellion" during the [[All Belarusian People's Assembly]]. [https://www.newsweek.com/belarus-stands-russia-protests-peace-war-1568744 (''Newsweek'')]
*[[China–United Kingdom relations]], [[Censorship in China]]
**[[China]]'s [[National Radio and Television Administration]] bans [[BBC World News]], in response to British [[telecommunications]] regulator [[Ofcom]] revoking the television license for the state-run [[China Global Television Network]] last week. [https://www.dw.com/en/china-bans-bbc-world-news/a-56540684 (DW)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Hellenic Parliament|Greek parliament]] approves legislation to create a [[special police]] force in [[List of universities in Greece|universities]]. The measure faces opposition from various [[Student society|student groups]], who describe it as "[[Criticism of democracy|anti-democratic]]". [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/world/greek-parliament-approves-plan-for-police-at-universities-14176862 (AFP via CNA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[National Emergency Concerning the Southern Border of the United States]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] ends former President [[Donald Trump]]'s nearly two-year emergency declaration on the [[Mexico–United States border]]. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/02/11/biden-trump-national-emergency-border-468603 (''Politico'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
**The [[German Badminton Association]] (DBV) cancels the upcoming 2021 [[German Open (badminton)|German Open]] in [[Mülheim an der Ruhr]] scheduled for March 9 to 14 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [https://www.kompas.com/badminton/read/2021/02/11/20422948/breaking-news-german-open-2021-resmi-dibatalkan (''Kompas'')]
*[[2020 FIFA Club World Cup]]
**[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] defeats [[Tigres UANL]] 1–0 in the [[2020 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] to win the [[FIFA Club World Cup]]. [[Robert Lewandowski]] is awarded the [[FIFA Club World Cup awards#Golden Ball|Golden Ball]] of the tournament. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/02/11/football/bayern-munich-club-world-cup-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
